challenge.method: Tested whether a downstream text combining the Apache heading with LLVM or Swift additions could be mistaken for the reference edition. Checked the publisher, pinned file, definition of “License,” end of terms, and the material following it.
challenge.results: The Foundation file bounds the terms at sections 1–9. Its appendix gives instructions and a sample notice with placeholders. It contains no LLVM or Swift addendum. A shared heading in a project file would identify the base edition but would leave any additional permission and its reach to be established from that project’s own text.

limitations: “Active” records the intended editorial registry mapping. January 2004 is the date printed in the heading.

The available sources contain neither LLVM’s nor Swift’s project publication. Their exact added wording, publisher attribution, inline scope, and coverage of individual files remain unverified. A particular work’s grant requires evidence for that work.
The policy documents were inspected at the specified commit. The adopted bundle digest was supplied and was not independently recomputed.
reasoning: The Apache Software Foundation publishes the reference text in its website repository. The heading reads “Apache License” and “Version 2.0, January 2004.” Section 1 defines the License by reference to sections 1 through 9, which include the copyright and patent grants. That text supports the Index classification as a license. SCES-1.0 §§1–4 require direct inspection, authority for the exact edition, six checks per supporting binding, and a targeted challenge to an identity merge. I applied those requirements and protocol stage 7 using the three policy documents at commit ab26f278422772f2d9e5d4dd016407d14372a710.
